paper_metadata.title: Achieving ultra-high strength in a precipitation-hardened CoCrNi-based medium-entropy alloy with partially recrystallized microstructure and heterogeneous grains

evidence.quote: A η*-Ni6(Al,Ti)Nb strengthened CoCrNi-based medium-entropy alloy with partially recrystallized and heterogeneous grain microstructure was prepared.

The alloy ingots (100 g) with a nominal composition of Co36Ni36Cr20Al3Ti2Nb3 (at%) were prepared by arc melting (≧ 99.99%) of pure raw materials under high-purity argon atmosphere. Nb was added through Ni50Nb50 (wt%) master alloy. To promote compositional homogeneity, every ingot was re-melted 5 times.
All ingots were solution-treated at 1200 °C for 2 h followed by water-quenching (WQ).

Based on these results, we conclude that precipitates in the UFG and CG regions are the same phase with hexagonal crystal structure (D024) similar to that of the η-Ni3Ti phase and with the Ni6(Al,Ti)Nb composition.
η*-Ni6(Al,Ti)Nb is introduced into HEA/MEA in two forms, as irregular blocks in the UFG region and lamellar shapes in the CG region.
The region on the left has the smallest grain size (~0.8 μm). Therefore, it was named as “ultra-fine grain (UFG)” region.
The middle region, marked as “coarse grain (CG)”, presents larger grains with average size of several microns.

For the region on the right-hand-side in Fig. 1 (c), it appears that a single grain exists and no indication of recrystallized grains can be found. It suggests that deformed grains are retained after the thermomechanical procedures. This region was called “Non-recrystallized grain (NRG)” region.
Fig. 1 (g) reveals that annealing twins (as demonstrated by the SAED pattern) formed in the CG region.
Fig. 1 (i) shows the microstructure of NRG region and it is observed that the NRG region has a typical deformation structure with high density dislocations.
Due to its single FCC phase, the A1 alloy shows low strength and excellent ductility with YS = 382 MPa, UTS (ultimate tensile strength) = 655 MPa and EL = 52%.

The high UTS is attributed to the high strain hardening rate. The high strain hardening rate of the A2 alloy can be explained based on Fig. 4. At the beginning of deformation, dislocation slip did not occur and deformation relied on SF. This cannot lead to severe deformation, so that deformation is difficult in the early stage.
